issues.detail: Hebrew 'רוּחוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם' means 'winds of heaven' (four winds), but Chinese renders '天的四靈' ('four spirits of heaven'), changing 'winds' to 'spirits'.

Hebrew 'וְלֹא כְמָשְׁלוֹ אֲשֶׁר מָשָׁל' means 'not according to his dominion which he ruled' (i.e., not with the same power/dominion as before), but Chinese '也不像那曾掌權的' ('nor like the one who once ruled') shifts the subject from the kingdom's dominion to a person, altering the meaning.

Chinese '而非獨自存留' ('rather than remaining alone') adds a concept not present in Hebrew 'מִלְּבַד אֵלֶּה' ('apart from these'), which simply means 'to others besides these' — the Chinese phrase introduces an idea of solitary survival not in the source.
